properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 20 at 2:52PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.1 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 3.0 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday, 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday,
2.3 ft above normal (8.1 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.9 ft
above normal (8.7 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 3.0 ft above
normal (8.8 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.6 ft above
normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions
include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical
tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes
earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San
Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 12:26PM PST until November 21 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may
cause major flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides if
storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf
arrive during high tide periods.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County, especially for areas in
and around Humboldt Bay.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 10 AM PST
Saturday with high tide at 8:31 AM on Saturday at the Humboldt
Bay North Spit tide gauge. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from
Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at
9:06 AM on Sunday, 9:44 AM on Monday, 10:25 AM on Tuesday,
11:09 AM on Wednesday, 11:56 AM on Thursday, 12:48 AM on
Friday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 12:14PM PST until November 25 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to
10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely
continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected.
For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding
possible.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches. Impacts highest across west to northwest-
facing beaches, including Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes,
as well as the Cayucos, Pismo, and Avila Piers.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to
3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will
likely be needed into Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

predictions based on trends in recent observations.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 10:56AM PST until November 24 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM
PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday
through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase
next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be
Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides
each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2
feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5
feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into
Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday.
NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical
predictions based on trends in recent observations.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Cold Weather Advisory issued November 20 at 7:51AM PST until November 21 at 8:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Cold conditions with temperatures as low as 33 to 36 degrees
expected.

* WHERE...The East Bay.

* WHEN...From 1 AM to 8 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Cold conditions will be hazardous, especially for
vulnerable populations. Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia
for people and animals.
properties.instruction:
Ensure portable heaters are working properly and are used correctly
to avoid sparking a fire indoors. Do not use generators or grills
inside as carbon monoxide poisoning can result.

Check with your local, city, or county officials for information on
available warming centers.

Be sure to dress in layers if outdoors. Make sure that pets and
livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.
